occurrences.checkable_against: Figure 2 estimates, Treasury issuance data, and Federal Reserve liquidity as a share of GDP

occurrences.quote_span: This relationship is particularly strong for net coupon issuance—$50 billion in net coupon issuance is associated with an increase in the TGCR-IORB spread of less than 1 basis point when aggregate liquidity is greater than 12 percent of nominal GDP but almost 10 basis points when aggregate liquidity is less than 10 percent of nominal GDP.
occurrences.speaker: Sriya Anbil, Alyssa Anderson, Lucy Cordes, and Romina Ruprecht
occurrences.subject: Federal Reserve Board staff analysis of repo markets and balance sheet

occurrences.checkable_against: Table 1 regression results and Treasury issuance data

figure.unit: basis points per $100 billion of net coupon and bill issuance, respectively

occurrences.quote_span: The statistically significant coefficients on net Treasury coupon and bill issuance indicate that $100 billion of issuance results in increases in repo rates of 3.9 and 1.3 basis points, respectively.
occurrences.speaker: Sriya Anbil, Alyssa Anderson, Lucy Cordes, and Romina Ruprecht
occurrences.subject: Federal Reserve Board staff analysis of repo markets and balance sheet

occurrences.checkable_against: Table 2 Column 3 regression results

figure.unit: basis points EFFR per 1 basis point TGCR increase at 8 percent liquidity/GDP

occurrences.quote_span: For example, based on Column 3 estimates, when liquidity is at 8 percent of GDP, a 1 basis point increase in TGCR leads to a 0.03 basis point increase in EFFR (0.092 - 0.75×0.08 = 0.032).

occurrences.checkable_against: Figure 2 estimates and Federal Reserve liquidity data
occurrences.quote_span: The estimated repo rate sensitivity to issuance is near zero, on average, when Federal Reserve liquidity is high relative to GDP but is positive at lower levels of liquidity.

occurrences.subject: Federal Reserve Board staff analysis of repo markets and balance sheet

occurrences.checkable_against: FHLB repo and federal funds lending records and corresponding rate data
occurrences.quote_span: Given that FHLBs have the option to lend in the repo market instead of the federal funds market, upward pressure on repo rates can spill over to the federal funds market as FHLBs can shift their lending from federal funds to repo markets when repo rates are more attractive, creating arbitrage pressure that pulls federal funds rates higher.
